correctness.rationale: Both centering matrices are Euclidean orthogonal projections, and P images the edge cube into the complete-bipartite cycle space. The exact four-term variance decomposition yields the two conditional sum-of-squares parity lower bounds and necessary-and-sufficient equality conditions. Checkerboard, opposite-paired columns, transposition, and balanced cyclic shift witnesses attain the bound in all even/odd cases. Strict convexity excludes all nonvertex outer contacts; triangle equality gives antipodal diametral pairs; a diametral pair pins down the unique enclosing-sphere center. Exact rational verification covers 2,401 explicit size pairs and exhaustive sign matrices in thirteen small cases; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The orthogonal projection of a graph edge cube is a canonical Euclidean cographic zonotope, and its maximum cycle-flow norm is a natural geometric/functional invariant. The theorem determines that invariant for the entire two-parameter biclique family, with nontrivial sharp odd-parity/aspect-ratio transitions, all outer contacts, all diametral pairs and unique circumsphere. This is mathematically motivated geometry beyond standard projector computation, not an arbitrary small enumeration.
